extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy (especially philosophy of physics and epistemology) and logically-minded readers interested in the foundations of physical concepts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and conceptual criteria for building the concepts of physical science (space, time, matter, things, persistence) out of sense-data and correlated appearances, together with methodological rules for when to infer entities versus construct them logically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological maxim: substitute logical constructions for inferred entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever possible, logical constructions are to be substituted for inferred entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by mathematical examples (irrationals defined as classes of ratios, cardinals as classes of equally numerous collections). The method: observe required properties of supposed inferred entities from the propositions that mention them, construct a logical function of less hypothetical entities with those properties, substitute that for the inferred entity to obtain a less doubtful interpretation. This method should be applied in the philosophy of physics to avoid unnecessary metaphysical postulates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principles for unavoidable inferences
rubrics_metrics.description: When inferences cannot be avoided they should be (1) made perfectly explicit and formulated in the most general manner possible, and (2) involve inferred entities similar to those given, not remote metaphysical constructs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inferred entities allowed here are of two kinds: (a) sense-data of other people (supported by testimony and analogical argument), and (b) 'sensibilia' that would appear in places with no minds (a hypothetical scaffolding). The former is likely acceptable; the latter is a provisional hypothesis to aid preliminary statements of physics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'physical'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Physical' means what is dealt with by physics—the constituents of the actual world as invoked by physics, whatever their ultimate nature may prove to be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an operational, working definition in preliminary discussions; details of what physics will finally count as physical may change, but this is the working sense for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'mental'
rubrics_metrics.description: A particular is 'mental' when it is aware of something; a fact is 'mental' when it contains a mental particular as a constituent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admits difficulty and controversy about the term; the paper assumes this dogmatic definition for present purposes and notes mental and physical are not necessarily mutually exclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat sense-data as physical constituents
rubrics_metrics.description: Sense-data (sensibilia) should be regarded as part of the subject-matter of physics (i.e., physical), even if they may also be mental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: a sense-datum is an object or particular the subject is aware of but does not contain the subject; hence its existence is not logically dependent on the subject. Distinguishing sense-data from sensations (the latter are mental complexes including the subject) removes chief obstacles to treating sense-data as physical. Non-persistence after ceasing to be data is an empirical inference and does not entail that they are mental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between sense-data and sensations
rubrics_metrics.description: Sense-data are external particulars (the objects of awareness); sensations are facts consisting in the subject's awareness of sense-data and are therefore mental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sense-data may be in the subject's body but the body is a material object distinct from the subject. The subjectivity of sense-data is physiological rather than psychical; recognising this helps treat sense-data as physical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Occam's razor: identify 'thing' with class of its appearances
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of postulating a substratum underlying different appearances, identify the 'thing' with the whole class of its appearances whenever this suffices for explanatory purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the class of appearances serves the purposes for which the notion of a 'thing' was invented, postulating an underlying substance is an unnecessary entity. This mirrors similar eliminations in the philosophy of mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-place ambiguity of 'place': distinguish 'place at' and 'place from'
rubrics_metrics.description: Every sense-datum has two associated 'places': (a) the place at which it appears (a place in private space) and (b) the place from which it appears (the perspective in perspective-space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These belong to different spaces (private spaces for each percipient, and a space of perspectives whose elements are whole private worlds). Recognising this resolves apparent paradoxes about incompatible simultaneous appearances and supports treating different observers' appearances as physically real.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of perspective-space and correlation principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Order the whole private worlds (perspectives) into a perspective-space by correlating 'sensibilia' that are regarded as different appearances of the same thing across perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical fact: the spatial order of correlated sensibilia in one perspective is nearly identical to that in another, allowing a three-dimensional ordering of perspectives (e.g., using variations in apparent size, shape). This construction yields the all-embracing space of physics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'thing' and 'appearances of one thing'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'thing' can be identified with the class of its appearances (including possible appearances to other perspectives); 'appearances of one thing' are correlated sensibilia across perspectives taken to be appearances of the same thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grouping of appearances relies on similarity, continuity, and correlations discovered by movement and testimony; includes appearances that are only hypothetical on grounds of continuity and resemblance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tentative definition of 'matter'
rubrics_metrics.description: The matter of a given thing is the limit of its appearances as their distance from the thing diminishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledged as a tentative and not fully satisfactory definition because empirically we cannot obtain such a limit from sense-data; it should be refined by further constructions and definitions. Motivation: nearer appearances are less affected by intervening matter, so the limiting appearance suggests what the thing 'really is' and underlies causal laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of single time: grouping appearances and conventional synchronization
rubrics_metrics.description: The one all-embracing time is a construction; appearances in different biographies (perspective-based histories) are grouped as constituting what a thing is at a moment, and synchronization across biographies is partly conventional (e.g., assuming velocities of sound/light).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventional choices are motivated by desiderata such as making simultaneity transitive (events simultaneous with the same event are simultaneous with one another) and convenience in formulating causal laws. Practical synchronization uses assumptions like constant propagation velocities to correlate times in different biographies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for persistence / identity over time: continuity plus dynamical conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: To regard appearances at different times as belonging to the same piece of matter requires (1) continuity (connected by a series of intermediate appearances) and (2) conformity with the laws of dynamics; continuity alone is not sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuity is often hypothetical (we do not observe continuously) and must be supplemented by dynamical considerations. For many ordinary objects continuity may suffice, but for cases like fluids or homogeneous masses dynamical laws are necessary to determine identity of matter over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for inferred 'sensibilia' as methodological scaffolding
rubrics_metrics.description: It is permissible to postulate 'sensibilia' that would appear in places without minds as a hypothetical scaffolding useful in constructing physics, but they need not be dogmatic elements in final theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such inferred sensibilia are provisional aids to build constructions (e.g., in constructing perspective-space or matter) and may be removed if physics can ultimately dispense with them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epistemic status of private worlds and testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: No sensibile is ever a datum to two people at once; each person lives in a private world and correlating private spaces into a common physical space relies on movement, similarity of data, and testimony about other people's appearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sense in which we accept the sense-data of others is ultimately analogical (argument for other minds); testimony supplies evidence allowing us to infer sense-data in other perspectives when logical economy recommends it.
